source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Astika sub-parva, adhyayas 36–40 (Parikshit's hunt, the silent sage Shamika, the dead snake, Shringin's curse, the palace on one pillar, Takshaka in the fruit)
structure: Every episode: RECAP (≈3 s; KIT.series.recapStrip) → HOOK (one question, Sauti at the Naimisha fire; the episode title follows it: KIT.series.episodeTitle) → STORY → NEXT (a cliffhanger line, then the teaser card: KIT.series.nextTeaser).

voice.note: speaker → script/cast.json (voice, speed, pitch). Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice, used by the timeline), say (what is spoken, if not `text`): '…' and '—' pause, ',' and '.' pause a little, [p:400] pauses 400 ms, {s:0.8} speaks what follows at 0.8× until the next {s:…} ({s} resets). captionY (px or "high") lifts the caption above low action.

lines.text: Uttanka urged King Janamejaya to avenge his father.
lines.note: RECAP. Episode 6's key image as a memory: Uttanka pointing at the enthroned king in the saffron court, a cold green hood in the lamp smoke. beats = 'urged', 'avenge'
lines.say: Uttanka urged King Janamejaya {s:1.06}to avenge his father.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: How did Takshaka kill King Parikshit?
lines.note: HOOK (Sauti, at the Naimisha fire, close). In the smoke: a cold green hood, then a crowned king's profile. beats = 'Takshaka' (the hood), 'Parikshit' (the king's profile, his name in gold); the episode title shows in the post

lines.text: King Parikshit, weary from the hunt, lost a wounded deer.
lines.say: King Parikshit, weary from the hunt, [p:80] lost a wounded deer.
lines.note: STORY 1. NEW PLACE: the forest at noon, white-hot glare through the trees. The deer, an arrow in its flank, bounds away into the trees; the king follows on foot, bow in hand, slowing. beats = 'Parikshit' (name label), 'hunt', 'deer' (it vanishes)

lines.speaker: parikshit
lines.text: Sage, where did the deer go?
lines.say: Sage… [p:100] where did the deer go?
lines.note: STORY 2 (Parikshit speaks). Shamika's hermitage among the cows: the sage sits in meditation, eyes closed; the king, breathless, stands over him and asks. beats = 'Sage', 'deer'

lines.text: But Shamika was under a vow of silence.
lines.note: STORY 3. Close on Shamika, eyes closed, still as stone; a lilac stillness round him; the king's shadow falls over him. beats = 'Shamika' (name label), 'silence' (everything hushes)

lines.text: Angry, the king draped a dead snake on him.
lines.say: Angry, [p:80] the king draped a dead snake on him.
lines.note: STORY 4. The king hooks a dead snake from the grass on his bow's tip and lays it across the sage's shoulders; the sage does not move. beats = 'Angry' (wrath ember), 'snake' (lifted), 'draped'

STORY 5. NEW PLACE: a river at dusk, red sky. The young ascetic Shringin turns, his rim kindling to vermilion; he scoops water in his palm (the curse is sealed with water). beats = 'Shringin' (name label), 'cursed'

lines.speaker: shringin
lines.text: In seven days, Takshaka will burn this king!
lines.say: In seven days, [p:250] Takshaka will burn this king!
lines.note: STORY 6 (Shringin speaks). He flings the water: seven drops hang in the air and become seven gold suns (the days); behind him, a cold green hood rises against the red. beats = 'seven' (the seven marks), 'Takshaka' (the hood), 'burn'

STORY 7. Back at the hermitage at evening, Shamika, the snake set down beside him, bows his head in sorrow; he sends his disciple running toward the distant city. beats = 'Shamika', 'warned' (the disciple runs)

lines.text: The king hid in a palace on one pillar, guarded by healers and mantras.
lines.say: The king hid in a palace on one pillar, guarded by healers and mantras.
lines.note: STORY 8. NEW PLACE: the palace on one pillar, moonlit, cold blue-silver night. A tall pillar rising from a moat, a pavilion on top with the king's lamp; guards with spears, healers with herbs, priests chanting (gold mantra syllables orbit the pavilion). beats = 'palace', 'pillar', 'mantras'

lines.text: On the seventh day, serpents came as hermits, bearing fruit.
lines.say: On the seventh day, serpents came as hermits, bearing fruit.
lines.note: STORY 9. Sunset of the seventh day: seven day-marks, six dim, the seventh blazing. Three hermits with offering-trays walk to the pillar; their shadows on the ground are serpents. beats = 'seventh' (the seventh mark lights), 'serpents' (the shadows), 'fruit'

lines.text: In one fruit crawled a tiny copper insect.
lines.note: STORY 10. Close: the king's hand turns a fruit in the lamplight; a tiny copper insect with black eyes crawls out onto his fingertip, glinting green. beats = 'fruit', 'copper', 'insect'

lines.text: It became Takshaka, and burned the king with his venom.
lines.say: It became Takshaka… and burned the king with his venom.
lines.note: STORY 11. The insect swells into the serpent king; his coils rise round the pavilion; he strikes; a stylised wall of green-gold venom-fire (mural flames, no gore) fills the pavilion; the king's crown falls. beats = 'Takshaka' (he grows), 'burned' (strike: fire), 'venom'

lines.text: His son would answer with fire.
lines.note: NEXT 1. The fallen crown in the ashes at dawn; it dissolves into young Janamejaya's crowned profile, lit from below by a rising sacrificial fire. beats = 'son', 'fire'
the teaser card (KIT.series.nextTeaser), with a glimpse of episode 8: the priests' great fire, serpents drawn down through the air into it
